explanation: $K_1 = hc/4000 - \phi = 3.1 - \phi$. $K_2 = hc/2000 - \phi = 6.2 - \phi$. Given $K_2 = 3K_1 \Rightarrow 6.2 - \phi = 3(3.1 - \phi) \Rightarrow 6.2 - \phi = 9.3 - 3\phi \Rightarrow 2\phi = 3.1 \Rightarrow \phi = 1.55$ eV.

question_text: In Young's double slit experiment, white light is used. The separation between the slits is d. The screen is at a distance D ($D \gg d$) from the slits. Some wavelengths are missing exactly in front of one of the slits. One of these wavelengths is
explanation: Position exactly in front of a slit is $y = d/2$. For missing wavelengths (minima): $y = (2n-1) \lambda D / 2d \Rightarrow d/2 = (2n-1) \lambda D / 2d \Rightarrow \lambda = d^2 / D(2n-1)$. For $n=1$, $\lambda = d^2/D$.
